matrix.zone.under_mev_desc: Below baseline targets. Great for recovery or lighter weeks.
matrix.zone.progressive_desc: Approaching target volume. A solid base for steady progress.
matrix.zone.optimal_mav_desc: In the target zone. An effective sweet spot for muscle building.
matrix.zone.high_fatigue_desc: Above standard target. Good for focus phases, but keep an eye on fatigue.
matrix.zone.over_mrv_desc: Well above usual targets. Consider giving this muscle group extra recovery.
matrix.info.title: Volume Reference Guide
matrix.info.overviewText: Tracks your weekly working sets across 18 muscle groups against benchmark volume targets. It provides a clear visual guide for muscle balance and workload—not a diagnosis of recovery or fatigue, which varies by sleep, nutrition, and experience.
matrix.info.directSetsDesc: Primary target muscles get full credit (1.0 set). For example, your chest receives full credit on a bench press.
matrix.info.indirectSetsDesc: Assisting muscles get half credit (0.5 set)—like your triceps and front shoulders supporting a bench press.
matrix.info.zonesSubtitle: Benchmark ranges to help guide your training
matrix.info.zoneUnderMevDetail: Below baseline targets. Good for a planned deload or active rest, though you may want more sets here if this muscle is a growth priority.
matrix.info.zoneProgressiveDetail: Steady building zone. A solid amount of work that stimulates progress without piling on excessive fatigue.
matrix.info.zoneOptimalMavDetail: The sweet spot for most lifters. This range typically drives the best balance of muscle gains and manageable recovery.
matrix.info.zoneHighFatigueDetail: High workload zone. Pushes muscles hard for short focus blocks, but watch your recovery and sleep if you stay here long.
matrix.info.zoneOverMrvDetail: Very high volume. Sets beyond this point often add more soreness than progress. Consider dialing back or taking a lighter week soon.
matrix.info.tipText: Use these ranges as a flexible guide alongside how your body actually feels. If an ongoing week is below target or a priority muscle is in the high zone, adjust based on your energy and goals, not just to match colors.

form_lab.info_brzycki_epley_desc: Brzycki and Epley estimate your one-repetition maximum (1RM) from logged working sets of 1–10 reps. Warm-up sets and sets of 11 or more reps are excluded from these estimates but stay in your history. These are estimates, not tested maximums or prescribed loads. Sets stopped with reps in reserve do not establish your maximum capacity.
form_lab.info_antagonist_desc: Compares logged working sets across movement patterns and muscle groups, such as push/pull and quadriceps/hamstrings. These ratios describe training distribution, not posture, joint health or recovery. Use them as a programming reference; a plan that prioritizes one area may have different ratios.
form_lab.info_mirror_desc: Forced Rep does not operate user databases. On Android, choose a cloud-backed folder for off-device backup; your storage provider controls its sync.

progression.rationale.insufficient_data: The latest log does not provide a complete baseline for this plan. Log all {sets} working sets with weights and reps.
progression.rationale.repeat_ceiling: Repeat these weights for {ceiling} reps per set. Confirm the same result in another workout before adding weight.
progression.rationale.load_step_unavaila: You reached the top of the rep range. Repeat the logged loads, or choose a small available increase yourself if manageable. No automatic load increase is offered for this baseline.
progression.info.rule_load: Reach the rep ceiling in every set twice at the same weights, within 21 days. Then try a small available increase while aiming to keep the same reps, if manageable. Use a smaller increase or repeat the load if reps or form suffer. No automatic increases for bodyweight or unsupported equipment.
progression.info.rule_reps: Keep each set’s weight. Try one more rep, up to the rep ceiling, if manageable.
progression.info.rule_hold: Below the rep minimum, add one rep at a time or go lighter. At the ceiling, repeat before adding weight. After more than 4 weeks away, repeat your last session first.
progression.info.rule_review: Review your plan when progress stalls. A lighter week is optional; no deload target is applied.
progression.rationale.first_session: No working-set baseline yet. Pick a manageable load for {reps} reps and log every working set.
progression.rationale.increase_load: All sets reached {ceiling} reps in two workouts. Try the new weights for {targetReps} reps; repeat the previous weights if reps or form suffer.
progression.rationale.increase_load_mixe: All sets reached {ceiling} reps in two workouts. Try the new weights for {targetReps} reps; repeat the previous weights if reps or form suffer.
progression.rationale.add_reps: Keep each set’s logged load. Try one more rep on each set below {ceiling}, if manageable. Effort is not measured.
progression.rationale.add_reps_mixed: Keep each set’s own logged load. Try one more rep on each set below {ceiling}, if manageable. Effort is not measured.
progression.rationale.hold_load: Your last session was below the prescribed minimum ({floor}). Try just one more rep per set at the logged loads if manageable. If the minimum remains difficult, consider a lighter load.
progression.rationale.hold_load_mixed: Some sets were below the prescribed minimum ({floor}). Keep each set’s own load and try just one more rep if manageable. If the minimum remains difficult, consider a lighter load.
progression.rationale.plateau: No rep gain across {sessions} full sessions at the same loads. Review your plan and how training feels; a lighter week is optional. Logs alone do not establish a need to deload.
progression.rationale.unverified_jump: The latest session had an unusually large load increase. Repeat and confirm this performance before progressing further.
progression.rationale.stale_baseline: Your latest full log for this workout is more than 4 weeks old. Repeat those weights and reps to re-establish your baseline before adding reps or weight.
progression.deload.none_desc: Logged sets alone cannot tell whether you need a deload.
progression.deload.stagnant_desc: Several exercises show no load or rep gain across three logged sessions. Consider a lighter week if training feels hard to sustain; this is not a fatigue assessment.
progression.deload.weeks_desc: You logged training in six consecutive weeks. A lighter week is optional, depending on your goals and experience; this does not establish overload or injury risk.
progression.info.title: Auto-Progression & Deloads
progression.info.subtitle: Programming ideas based on your logged weights and reps
progression.info.ddpText: Targets use your latest full session from this workout day, or from another day with the same sets and rep range. Incomplete logs give no target. Warmups don’t count.
progression.info.plateauText: Only full sessions with matching weights and set counts are compared. Below the rep ceiling, three without a total rep gain prompt a review. The app doesn’t measure fatigue, recovery or technique.
progression.info.tipText: Follow your goals and how training feels. Logs don’t require a fixed deload schedule. A lighter week doesn’t guarantee progress or injury prevention.

today.restMotivation.0: Real progress is forged when recovery matches your effort. Sleep deeply, refuel to rebuild, and let your body adapt.
today.restMotivation.1: Rest is not the absence of training; it is the catalyst for growth. Give your muscles time to repair and supercompensate.
today.restMotivation.2: Muscles rebuild during rest, not in the gym. Stepping back today ensures you bring full intensity to the bar tomorrow.
today.restMotivation.3: Fatigue masks fitness. Allowing your central nervous system to reset is what turns hard volume into lasting strength.
today.restMotivation.4: Consistency includes knowing when not to train. Quality rest prevents joint wear and fuels continuous progressive overload.
today.restMotivation.5: Adaptation happens in the quiet hours between sessions. Hydrate, recover, and prepare your body for the next challenge.
today.restMotivation.6: Growth occurs when recovery meets discipline. Recharge fully today so you can attack the upcoming training week with conviction.

onboarding.goal.strength.desc: Add weight to key compound lifts (squat, bench, deadlift).
onboarding.goal.maintain.title: Stay Fit & Consistent
onboarding.goal.maintain.desc: Maintain fitness, stay healthy, and build a lasting routine.
onboarding.experience.title: What is your lifting experience?
onboarding.experience.subtitle: We will tune exercise complexity and volume accordingly.
onboarding.experience.beginner.title: Beginner (< 1 year)
onboarding.experience.beginner.desc: Learning the movements and building basic gym confidence.
onboarding.experience.intermediate.title: Intermediate (1–3 years)
onboarding.experience.intermediate.desc: Consistent training history, familiar with barbells and progression.
onboarding.experience.advanced.title: Advanced (3+ years)
onboarding.experience.advanced.desc: Comfortable with high volume, varied splits, and intensity.
onboarding.equipment.title: Where will you train?
onboarding.equipment.subtitle: Select the gear you have reliable access to.
onboarding.equipment.commercialGym.title: Commercial Gym
onboarding.equipment.commercialGym.desc: Full access to barbells, racks, dumbbells, cables, and machines.
onboarding.equipment.machinesOnly.title: Machines & Cables Only
onboarding.equipment.machinesOnly.desc: Selectorized machines and cables with low barrier to entry.
onboarding.equipment.dumbbellsHome.title: Home / Dumbbells Only
onboarding.equipment.dumbbellsHome.desc: Adjustable dumbbells and an adjustable bench (no barbell or rack).
onboarding.equipment.bodyweightHome.desc: Floor space, a wall or counter, a sturdy chair and a step.
onboarding.equipment.pullUpBarHome.title: Home / Pull-Up Bar
onboarding.equipment.pullUpBarHome.desc: A securely installed pull-up bar, plus floor space, a chair and a step.
onboarding.frequency.title: How many days can you train?
onboarding.frequency.subtitle: Consistency matters more than cramming too many days.
onboarding.frequency.days2.title: 2 Days / Week
onboarding.frequency.days2.desc: Minimal and sustainable. Two full-body sessions for busy weeks.
onboarding.frequency.days3.title: 3 Days / Week
onboarding.frequency.days3.desc: Manageable and high-recovery. Great for full-body or athletic splits.
onboarding.frequency.days4.title: 4 Days / Week
onboarding.frequency.days4.desc: The sweet spot. Balanced upper/lower splits with plenty of recovery.
onboarding.frequency.days5.title: 5 Days / Week
onboarding.frequency.days5.desc: High dedication. Dedicated muscle group sessions with focused intensity.
onboarding.frequency.days6.title: 6 Days / Week
onboarding.frequency.days6.desc: Pure Push, Pull, Legs frequency for experienced, high-recovery lifters.
onboarding.schedule.title: Which days do you prefer to train?
onboarding.schedule.subtitle: Pick {count} days that best match your weekly lifestyle.
onboarding.rec.title: We built your plan.
onboarding.rec.subtitle: Here is the optimal program matched to your goals, space, and schedule.
onboarding.reason.homeForge: Matched for home training with dumbbells and an adjustable bench with balanced frequency.
onboarding.reason.bodyweightBase: Matched for home training without equipment: three short full-body sessions you progress with harder variations.
onboarding.reason.barFloor: Matched for home calisthenics with a pull-up bar: upper/lower sessions four days a week.
onboarding.reason.essentials: Matched for two full-body gym sessions that practise every main movement pattern twice a week.
onboarding.reason.machineFoundation: Matched for machine and cable guidance with low joint impact and zero barbell setup required.
onboarding.reason.classicPpl: Matched for 6 days of dedicated Push, Pull, and Legs training with high hypertrophy volume.
onboarding.reason.aestheticHypertrophy: Matched for 5-day balanced upper/lower physique development with extra shoulder focus.
onboarding.reason.powerbuildingStrength: Matched for 4-day heavy compound progression (squat, bench, deadlift) paired with hypertrophy accessory work.
onboarding.reason.upperLower: Matched for 4-day upper/lower balance hitting each major muscle group twice a week with optimal recovery.
onboarding.reason.athleticPerformance: Matched for 3-day power, explosiveness, and athletic movement patterns.
onboarding.reason.fullBodyClassic: Matched for 3-day whole-body training repeating key movement patterns with high efficiency.
onboarding.reason.default: Matched to your selected training preferences and schedule.

form_lab.info_cloud_desc: Saves a local copy of your programs and history. When iCloud Drive is available, writes a copy to your private container; iCloud controls off-device upload.
